description: Hi! We're a team of 4 from Egypt passionate about space, nutrition and making science fun for kids. We're building AstroNutri, a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer game where players run a lunar outpost and balance food, power, water & radiation shielding through nutrition decisions across 4 mission phases. We have a strong science and tech core and we're open to meeting motivated teammates who love games, design, storytelling and space exploration. Let's build something impactful together!
summary:
AstroNutri is an interactive 3D educational adventure game designed for children aged 7–12, combining space exploration with healthy lifestyle education. We developed a four-level space mission where players take the role of a young astronaut, preparing for launch on Earth, traveling through a zero-gravity environment, operating a lunar outpost, and safely returning to Earth.
The game addresses the challenge of making scientific and health education more engaging and accessible to children. Through interactive mini-games and realistic mission scenarios, players learn about balanced nutrition, hydration, physical health, the effects of microgravity on the human body, astronaut safety, water recycling, and space exploration.
AstroNutri transforms complex scientific concepts into enjoyable, hands-on learning experiences, encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and informed decision-making. It is important because it connects space science with everyday healthy habits, helping children understand how science can improve their lives while inspiring the next generation of explorers.
details:
Live Interactive App (PWA): https://astronutri-nasa-space-adventure.vercel.app

Source Code Repository (GitHub): https://github.com/Abdallah-Selmi221/astronutri-nasa-space-adventure

1. What It Does & How It Works:

AstroNutri is an interactive 3D space simulation and eco-nutrition game spanning a 4-level space campaign (33 explorable locations and 21 hands-on mini-games) accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts:

- Level 1 (Earth Preparation): Players pack crumb-safe space rations (preventing floating debris from clogging air filters), inspect mission gear, complete medical checks, customize the modular SPACE-FIT X intra-vehicular suit (7 functional modules including joint resistance and personal radiation dosimetry), and execute pre-launch checklists.

- Level 2 (Zero-G Transit): Players master inertia and handrail locomotion in 0.0g microgravity, secure floating hazards, hydrate from sealed pouches, manage space adaptation sickness, and navigate past Near-Earth Asteroids using live NASA NeoWs telemetry.

- Level 3 (Lunar Outpost Operations): At Shackleton Crater (0.16g), players perform resistance workouts against bone/muscle loss, maintain the ECLSS water recycling loop, cultivate a closed-loop Hydroponic Bio-Cabin (growing lettuce, arugula, and turnip alongside space-adapted Egyptian/Sinai foods like Sinai honey, date bars, and tahini pouches), and balance a 100-unit power budget between radiation shielding, water recovery, and crop lighting during a real NASA DONKI solar storm event.

- Level 4 (Return to Earth): Players secure lunar samples, navigate home under a realistic 1.3-second Earth–Moon communication delay, resolve in-flight emergencies, maintain a safe heat-shield re-entry corridor, and deploy parachutes for splashdown.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact:

AstroNutri bridges the gap between abstract space-biology research and experiential learning. Instead of passive reading, players experience real engineering trade-offs—such as power scarcity during solar storms, crumb containment, and closed-loop life support. Every scientific claim carries an explicit epistemic badge (Proven on ISS, Experimental Research, Planning Assumption, or Simplified Game Rule) so learners clearly distinguish validated ISS science from experimental research like Spirulina photobioreactors, inspiring critical scientific thinking across all ages.

3. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & 3D Engine: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (WebGL, GLTFLoader, InstancedMesh optimization), and Vite.

- 3D Modeling & Audio: Blender 5.3 (custom lightweight PBR .glb assets) and ElevenLabs API for Egyptian Arabic voice guidance ("Robo").

- NASA & Partner Data: NASA DONKI, NeoWs, OSDR, APOD, EPIC, LROC, ISS ECLSS documentation, and ESA MELiSSA research.

- Deployment & Architecture: Installable, offline-capable Progressive Web App (PWA) powered by Workbox runtime caching, automated Node.js/Chrome QA test suites, Git/GitHub, and Vercel cloud hosting.

4. Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered:

- Cultural & Scientific Fusion: Integrates locally inspired, nutrient-dense Egyptian/Sinai foods (Sinai honey, date bars, tahini) evaluated against real NASA space-food criteria alongside hydroponic crops.

- Accessibility & Performance: Engineered as a lightweight (< 5.2 MB initial precache) offline-first PWA running at 60 FPS on standard mobile and desktop browsers without requiring heavy app-store downloads, plus a built-in "Jury Demo Mode" in Settings to unlock all 21 missions instantly for evaluation.
